blessed sacrament chapel: emy rawson, the bosheen - remembrance history notes - part 146: the malt stores the main locations of the town’s malt stores were the quay and john street in times past. these buildings were in effect huge bulk stores with timber floors supported by strong beams to bear the weight of drying grain. the grain was barley for which south wexford and kilkenny were famous. this grain was purchased by the local malting family, roche & sons for conversion to malt via a drying and baking process. the finished malt was shipped by schooner from the quays of town to guinness brewery in dublin for manufacture of its famous stout. some names of these schooners spring to mind, including the de wadden and the harvest king. the loading of the malt into these schooners was by dockers who carried the open bags on their shoulders down the bouncing gang-plank to tip the contents into the ship’s hold. this was a skilled job as a missed step on the gang-plank could send bag and carrier into the tide. courtesy of jim sutton
